display.purpose: Landing hero only. Fluid: clamp(2.5rem, 1.6rem + 4vw, 4.25rem) — the clamp minimum is part of this step, not a separate one.

pageTitle.purpose: Every authenticated page h1, and the hanging quotation mark on a quote bubble. Fluid: clamp(1.75rem, 1.3rem + 1.8vw, 2.5rem).

sectionTitle.purpose: Profile sheet sections, modal titles, empty-state headings.

control.purpose: Form fields and the chat composer. 16px is a floor, not a preference — smaller values make iOS Safari zoom the viewport on focus.

body.purpose: Profile prose, chat text, card names.

label.purpose: The only all-caps metadata style in the product. Every section header and field label. 11px is the floor for tracked uppercase text.

code.purpose: The sole non-Nunito face, used only for inline code and code fences inside chat markdown. Must not spread to labels, data, or anything styled to look technical.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The product's only easing curve. Entrances fade and rise a few pixels; nothing overshoots. The old back-out curve cubic-bezier(0.175, 0.885, 0.32, 1.275) was removed.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Immediate state feedback such as hover fills.

motion.name: dur
motion.purpose: Default transition duration for colour and border changes.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The app's only call to action. Peach fill with peach ink at 8.6:1; the tint is never the text colour.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 20px; border-radius: 12px; border: 1px solid transparent; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), filter 150ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--peach, #fdba74); color: var(--peach-ink, #7c2d12); border-color: var(--lavender-border, rgba(91,33,182,0.22)); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus, #3b6fd4); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: A red wash rather than a red fill. Destructive actions announce themselves without shouting.

components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; min-height: 44px; min-width: 44px; padding: 0 20px; border-radius: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--red-border, rgba(200,30,30,0.22)); background: var(--red-bg, rgba(200,30,30,0.07)); color: var(--red-ink, #c81e1e); font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: var(--red-bg-hover, rgba(200,30,30,0.13)); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus, #3b6fd4); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: White, never tinted — a field should look like a hole punched in the paper, not a slightly different shade of it. Definition comes from the stronger hairline. The focus ring sits flush at -1px inset so the edge recolours instead of gaining a halo.
components.html: <input class="ds-field" type="text" placeholder="Type a tag and press Enter" />
components.css: .ds-field { display: block; width: 100%; min-height: 44px; padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border-mid, rgba(120,98,74,0.38)); background: var(--surface, #fff); color: var(--text-1, #292524); font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; transition: border-color 220ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-field::placeholder { color: var(--text-3, #6f6660); } .ds-field:hover:not(:disabled):not(:focus) { border-color: var(--text-3, #6f6660); } .ds-field:focus { border-color: var(--focus, #3b6fd4); outline: 2px solid var(--focus, #3b6fd4); outline-offset: -1px; } .ds-field:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Sticker Chip
components.description: Neutral paper metadata: genres, places, food restrictions, political views. The bulk of a profile is lists, and keeping them neutral is what lets the coloured things mean something.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(120,98,74,0.24)); background: var(--surface-2, #fbf7f1); color: var(--text-2, #57534e); font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Sticker Tag
components.description: Personality tags, always lavender. The same colour on the profile grid, the detail sheet, the edit form, and the PDF export — a tag is lavender because it is a tag, not because of where it renders.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--lavender-border, rgba(91,33,182,0.22)); background: var(--lavender-bg, rgba(196,181,253,0.22)); color: var(--lavender-ink, #5b21b6); font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Profile Card
components.description: One person in the browse grid. Lifts on hover by translating and darkening its border — never by a shadow. Its washi tape is keyed to the profile id, so someone keeps the same tape however the list is filtered.

Ser he/they

#Nerdy#Loyal
components.css: .ds-card { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; padding: 20px; border-radius: 16px; border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(120,98,74,0.24)); background: var(--surface, #fff); font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: border-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-card:hover { border-color: var(--border-mid, rgba(120,98,74,0.38)); transform: translateY(-6px); } .ds-card-tape { position: absolute; top: -5px; left: 50%; width: 38px; height: 20px; background: var(--lavender, #c4b5fd); opacity: 0; transform: translateX(-50%) rotate(1.8deg); clip-path: polygon(5% 0%, 95% 0%, 100% 50%, 95% 100%, 5% 100%, 0% 50%); transition: opacity 200ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-card:hover .ds-card-tape { opacity: 0.7; } .ds-card-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin-bottom: 14px; } .ds-card-avatar { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 44px; height: 44px; flex-shrink: 0; border-radius: 12px; background: var(--blue, #93c5fd); color: var(--blue-ink, #3b6fd4); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 800; transform: rotate(-3deg); } .ds-card-name { margin: 0; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text-1, #292524); } .ds-card-pronouns { margin-left: 6px; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text-3, #6f6660); text-transform: lowercase; } .ds-card-tags { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px; } .ds-card-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--lavender-border, rgba(91,33,182,0.22)); background: var(--lavender-bg, rgba(196,181,253,0.22)); color: var(--lavender-ink, #5b21b6); font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Sheet Section Heading
components.description: Signature component. A profile is one sheet of paper, and this is how it is divided: a strip of tape, a real title, and a hairline running out to the sheet's edge. No card, no icon tile. The tape colour belongs to the section, so reading a profile and editing one stay recognisably the same document.
components.html:
Favorites & interests

Sections are divided by a heading and a hairline, never by a new card.
components.css: .ds-sheet { padding: 28px 36px; border-radius: 28px; border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(120,98,74,0.24)); background: var(--surface, #fff); font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-section-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin-bottom: 20px; } .ds-tape-mark { display: block; flex-shrink: 0; width: 26px; height: 10px; background: var(--peach, #fdba74); clip-path: polygon(5% 0%, 95% 0%, 100% 50%, 95% 100%, 5% 100%, 0% 50%); } .ds-section-title { margin: 0; font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.25; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--text-1, #292524); } .ds-section-rule { flex: 1; height: 1px; background: var(--border, rgba(120,98,74,0.24)); } .ds-section-body { margin: 0; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--text-2, #57534e); }

components.name: Quote Bubble
components.description: Signature component. Reserved for things the person actually said — the hanging quotation mark is the one device meaning 'their words, not yours', which is why memories, notes, and the bio are plain wells and prose instead. Its expanded modal is the same fill and radius, but takes a 2px float line, because a 1px card hairline is invisible against the scrim.
components.css: .ds-quote { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 100%; padding: 16px 16px 16px 48px; border-radius: 16px; border: 1px solid var(--lavender-line, rgba(91,33,182,0.24)); background: var(--lavender-soft, #ede9fe); color: var(--text-2, #57534e); font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.625; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-quote:hover { border-color: var(--lavender, #c4b5fd); } .ds-quote:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus, #3b6fd4); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-quote-mark { position: absolute; left: 14px; top: 8px; font-size: 2.5rem; font-weight: 800; line-height: 1; color: var(--lavender-ink, #5b21b6); opacity: 0.4; pointer-events: none; user-select: none; }

components.name: Top Navigation
components.description: 56px of clean paper with one warm hairline beneath. Its brand and sign-out glyphs land on exactly the same pixel columns as the page content below, because both derive their edges from the shell's gutter token.

Nexia

components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; height: 56px; padding: 0 24px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(120,98,74,0.24)); background: var(--surface, #fff); font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-nav-brand { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 44px; padding: 0 8px; border-radius: 12px; color: var(--text-1, #292524); font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: -0.01em; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-nav-brand:hover { background: var(--surface-2, #fbf7f1); } .ds-nav-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; } .ds-nav-link { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 44px; min-width: 44px; padding: 0 12px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; background: transparent; color: var(--text-2, #57534e); font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-nav-link:hover { background: var(--surface-2, #fbf7f1); } .ds-nav-link-active { background: var(--surface-3, #f4ede3); color: var(--blue-ink, #3b6fd4); } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus, #3b6fd4); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
Nexia is a personal memory book, not a productivity dashboard. Screens should feel like a carefully kept slambook: warm paper, sticker chips, gentle colour, and small washi-tape details that make profiles feel kept rather than stored.

The material is paper, and paper is opaque. An earlier version of this system built every surface from translucent glass (backdrop-filter: blur(20px)). It was replaced wholesale: translucency muddied every card against the warm page, cost a compositing layer per element, and read as a tech product rather than a scrapbook. Depth now comes from opaque surfaces, warm hairlines, and spacing — and from nothing else. The product is flat and carries no shadows at all.

There is no backdrop-filter anywhere in the app, and none should be added.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream page, opaque white paper, restrained peach / lavender / blue accents.
Rounded panels separated by fine warm borders, never by a shadow.
Small tape and sticker motifs used for hierarchy, never as wallpaper.
Nunito throughout, with compact all-caps labels and calm body text.

rules.name: The One Shell Rule
rules.body: No page sets its own max-width or horizontal padding. If a surface needs to span the viewport (the form action bar, the navbar), it goes full-bleed and puts a PageShell inside itself.

rules.name: The Navbar Offset Rule
rules.body: Dashboard pages use .page-body (min-height: calc(100dvh - var(--navbar-h))), never min-h-screen. The latter overshoots by exactly the navbar height and forces a scrollbar on every page.

rules.name: The One Sheet Rule
rules.body: A profile is one sheet of paper — a single .paper article that runs from the hero to the last quote — on both the detail page and the edit form. It is not a stack of section cards. The earlier version gave every section its own white panel with a grey icon tile and an 11px caps label; four of those in a column is a settings screen wearing a scrapbook's colours, and it left section headings and field labels sharing one type size, so the page had no hierarchy to read. Sections are divided by a heading and a hairline, never by a new card. The same rule is why the form uses the same sheet: editing a profile and reading one are the same document in two states.

rules.name: The App Screen Lock
rules.body: Chat is the only screen that owns the viewport, and it adds .app-screen to <html> while mounted, which removes the document scroller entirely. Sizing the column to 100dvh is not sufficient on a phone: the document keeps a scroller of its own, so a flick past either end of the transcript chains into the page and drags the browser chrome — two scrollers competing for one gesture. The transcript additionally sets overscroll-behavior: contain. Any future full-height screen uses the same class; nothing else should.

rules.name: The Ink Rule (non-negotiable)
rules.body: peach, lavender, and blue are surface tints only. They are never a text or icon colour — all three fail contrast as a foreground on paper (blue on white measures 1.8:1). Every accent has an -ink variant that clears WCAG AA: peach-ink, lavender-ink, blue-ink, green-ink, red-ink. Use those for anything a person has to read.

rules.name: The Two Blues Rule
rules.body: blue-ink is tuned for white paper (4.8:1). On blue-soft it falls to 3.8:1 and fails, so text on the blue wash uses blue-ink-deep (7.0:1) instead. The two are not interchangeable; peach and lavender need no equivalent because their inks already clear AA on their own washes (8.0:1 and 7.5:1).

rules.name: The Content Colour Rule
rules.body: Colour is assigned by what a thing is, never by where it lands in a loop. A tag is lavender on the profile grid, on the detail sheet, in the form, and in the PDF export. The song someone is bound to is the one peach well. Ranked songs cycle lavender / peach / blue because rank is the information — and they carry their number too, so colour is never the only code. Everything else — genres, places, food, politics — stays a neutral paper chip, which is what lets the coloured things mean something. An index-modulo accent applied to whatever happens to render next is the failure mode this rule exists to prevent.

rules.name: The Accent Ration Rule
rules.body: If every card uses all three accents, the scrapbook stops feeling kept and starts feeling noisy.

rules.name: The Warm Light Rule
rules.body: page is the baseline for every surface. Dark mode is forbidden — PRODUCT.md specifies light theme only.

rules.name: The Focus Rule
rules.body: One focus treatment, set globally on :focus-visible: a 2px focus outline at 2px offset. Components must not remove it.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Nunito carries the product. No display face for app labels, buttons, forms, or profile content.

rules.name: The One Label Rule
rules.body: .t-label is the only all-caps metadata style. A second, smaller 10px label size existed on the detail page and was removed — 11px is the floor for tracked uppercase text.

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: Form controls never go below 16px on mobile.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow anywhere. Hover states that used to lift with a shadow (profile cards) now darken their border and rise a few pixels instead.

rules.name: The No Nested Paper Rule
rules.body: .paper inside .paper is never correct. Nested groups use .paper-sunk (a bordered surface-2 well).

rules.name: The Float Line Rule
rules.body: A hairline is only visible when it is darker than both surfaces it divides. On the page that happens for free — a card's line is darker than its own fill and darker than the cream behind it. On the overlay it does not: the scrim composites to a mid tone, so a normal 1px card border ends up lighter than the scrim and dissolves into the card's silhouette. A dialog that simply reuses its card's border therefore looks like it has no border at all. Surfaces floating on the scrim use line-float / lavender-line-float at 2px instead — the one place in the product where a border is not 1px, because it is the one place a border has to out-contrast a mid grey. overlay itself is 0.55, not 0.42; the lighter scrim sat too close to the paper it was meant to be pushing back.

dos: Do route every page through PageShell.
Do use an -ink colour for anything readable.
Do keep touch targets at 44px or larger.
Do hide empty profile sections rather than showing placeholders.
Do keep 16px on form controls at mobile widths.
Do let the loading skeleton use the loaded state's shell and padding, so nothing shifts when data arrives.
donts: Don't add backdrop-filter, glass, or blur as decoration.
Don't tint a form field — fields are white.
Don't put text or icons in peach, lavender, or blue.
Don't use min-h-screen on a page that sits under the navbar.
Don't hand-roll a button, field label, or container width.
Don't break a profile back into a stack of section cards.
Don't colour something by its index in a loop — colour it by what it is.
Don't paste tape on a surface that already carries a wash.
Don't give a button beside a field a fixed height.
Don't animate the same property in both CSS and Framer Motion.
Don't use emoji as an icon system — the app uses Lucide.
